checkpoint: Plain source native hydration and reconnect ownership, based on bc1e3913
changes: Initial React/Preact rendering hydrates the inline source where SSR placed it. Native mounted source ownership then transfers to an existing stable portal without a second application root or replacing the source DOM. Native class boundaries add no host wrapper.

Native source ranges retain live nodes, deferred hydration boundary markers, source state, native context and useId through destination changes. Delegated events follow the source parent while parked. Native Activity pause retains the mounted source; actual destruction disposes it.
Empty ordinary sources retain destination identity and fallbacks so returning text belongs to the original first placement. Scoped and authored lazy-template behavior stays fresh.

Compiled and handwritten accepting content share one filter. Rejected native elements and visible text are omitted after existing diagnostics; compiled entry keys and diagnostic ownership are preserved.

ProjectionClaims associates native position and effect lifetime. Paused owners preserve identity through whole-mount reconnect; permanent stop releases through the existing registration, including stop while paused. Static Node rendering skips pause tracking.

Negative browser bundle tests keep retained-source owners out of ordinary named/default button output. Existing table fixtures explicitly forward unclaimed attributes at their authored th destination; original output assertions remain intact.

proofBeforeFix.observation: Both existing public tests fail at baseline. React recovers the whole tree after template-vs-i mismatch; Preact silently replaces the original preedited input.
Intermediate positioning change produced SecondFallbackPlain instead of PlainSecondFallback. Earliest owned source/fallback/anchor lookup restores the unchanged manual structures.

Native React counter remained Context!!:2 after a programmatic click while every outlet was absent; expected Context!!:3. Preact direct-listener control passed. Retarget delegated listeners to the parking fragment.
Both targets rendered BorrowedFallback/Plain after empty text source returned; expected Plain/OwnFallback. Keep the borrowed destination while ordinary content is empty.
Original input disappeared after reveal. Native control establishes actual StrictMode effect pause/restart counts; retain the mounted range instead of treating layout pause as permanent destruction.
Hydrated original input was lost on first transfer because deferred server DOM had no child host fibers at initial capture. Include the native DehydratedFragment comment range.

Existing warning test showed native span and stray text in converted tr while live omitted them. Classifier warnings alone and classifier-only return changes did not affect the compiled raw-content path. Route both compiled and derived content through the same filter without reassigning compiled entries.

Shared own-first cases switched to borrowed placement after reconnect. Strengthened immediate post-reconnect assertion reproduces it before the later unrelated alias update. Preserve paused claim identity and release permanently stopped lifetimes.

qualificationLimits: Native C# source is unchanged. Its tests and complete Fluid output checks are regression evidence, not native hydration or performance qualification.
Native React/Preact ownership fields and serialization protocols are internal. Exact tested minima are recorded; future release compatibility remains a maintenance concern.

The native hydration/lifecycle cases use the development framework SSR/client builds. Production fresh-render coverage is supplied by the shared matrix; full production native SSR/lifecycle combinations remain part of whole-goal qualification.
React/Preact still use the older repeated-slot selection. Single conditional and accepting receiving variants need alignment to shared retainedSlotNames with correct decorated projection ownership.

Accepted presets, remaining setup/context/filtering boundaries, deeper native provider/streaming/namespace combinations and source-order forwarding/control interactions remain unqualified. No support exclusion is established by these limits.
Passing current table warnings, including existing unsupported preset behavior, does not prove complete accepted-preset semantics.
